localStorage چیه و چه فرقی با sessionStorage داره؟ لطفاً به انگلیسی جواب بده.

Both are browser storage APIs that persist key/value strings client-side.

- **localStorage** — survives page reloads and browser restarts, never expires, and is shared across all tabs of the same origin.
- **sessionStorage** — scoped to a single tab and cleared automatically when that tab closes.

```js
localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
localStorage.getItem('theme');   // 'dark'
localStorage.removeItem('theme');
localStorage.clear();
```

Common uses: localStorage for themes, language preference and drafts; sessionStorage for one-time tokens or multi-step form state.

Limits to keep in mind: about 5 MB per origin, strings only (use `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse`), synchronous API (huge writes can block the main thread), and never store secrets there — any script running on the page can read it.

**Symptom:** Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener').

**Root cause:** The script runs before the DOM element exists (script in <head> without defer) or the selector has a typo.

**Fix:**
```css
<script src="app.js" defer></script>
```

**Broken version:**
```css
<head><script src="app.js"></script></head> /* runs before <body> exists */
```

**Prevention:** Use defer (or put scripts at the end of body), and null-check the element in development.

What meta tags should every production page include for SEO?

```html
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

  <title>Arion Hosting — Fast Managed WordPress for Small Teams</title>
  <meta name="description"
        content="Managed WordPress hosting with automatic backups, global CDN and 24/7 support. 30-day money-back guarantee.">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://arionhost.example/plans">

  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow">
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any">
</head>
```

**Why this works:** `charset` must come first because the parser needs the encoding before it can decode the rest of the document. The `viewport` meta enables responsive layout on mobile; without it, phones render at a virtual 980px width and scale down. `<title>` (~50–60 chars) is the single strongest on-page ranking element and the text shown in search results and tabs. `description` is not a direct ranking factor but is usually used as the search snippet, so it drives click-through. `rel="canonical"` consolidates duplicate URLs (query strings, tracking params) onto one authoritative address so link equity is not split. Keep `robots` as `index, follow` (or omit it — that is the default) and only restrict specific pages that genuinely must stay out of the index.

**CSS box model — Beginner to Expert**

[Beginner]
Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin, from inside out.
```css
.box { width: 200px; padding: 16px; border: 2px solid #333; margin: 8px; }
```

[Intermediate]
Set `box-sizing: border-box` globally so declared width includes padding and border.
```css
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
```
Why it works: with `border-box`, `width: 200px` really renders 200px total, ending arithmetic surprises.

[Advanced]
Manage margin collapse: it happens between vertical margins of adjacent/parent-child blocks; prefer `gap` in flex/grid containers.
```css
.stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: gap is real space on the container, so it never collapses with child margins.

[Expert]
Use logical properties (`margin-block`, `padding-inline`) and `inset` shorthand for direction-aware boxes.
```css
.notice { padding-block: .75rem; padding-inline: 1rem; margin-block-end: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: logical properties follow the writing direction, so RTL layouts need no overrides.

Debug: My dropdown has z-index: 9999 but it still renders UNDER another element. Why does z-index not work?

**Symptom:** a huge `z-index` loses to a smaller one, or z-index seems ignored completely.

**Root causes — z-index only applies to positioned/flex/grid items, and only within its stacking context:**

1. **No position:** z-index is ignored on static elements.
```css
.dropdown { z-index: 9999; }                     /* ignored: static */
.dropdown { position: absolute; z-index: 9999; } /* now it applies */
```
2. **Trapped in a stacking context:** if a parent creates one (`position` + `z-index`, `opacity < 1`, `transform`, `filter`, `will-change`, `isolation`, `mix-blend-mode`), the dropdown's 9999 competes only INSIDE that parent. If the parent's own context sits below the rival, no child z-index can escape.
```css
.modal-wrap { position: absolute; opacity: 0.99; z-index: 1; } /* context A */
.sidebar    { position: relative; z-index: 10; }               /* context B beats ALL of A */
```

**Diagnosis:** in DevTools walk up the tree in the Elements panel checking Computed styles of each ancestor for `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `will-change`, `position/z-index` — the first ancestor creating a stacking context is the ceiling your element cannot rise above.

**Fix:** raise the z-index of the correct ANCESTOR (the stacking-context owner), or remove the accidental context-creating property (drop `opacity: 0.99`, delete an unused `transform`), or scope layers deliberately with `isolation: isolate`.

**Prevention:** keep a small z-index scale (10/20/30) instead of 9999 arms races; know which properties create stacking contexts before layering components; wrap self-contained widgets in `isolation: isolate` so their internals never leak out.
